issue_context.title: lightning: and data sample check, support check-only
issue_context.body:
## Feature Request
- add data sample check, mainly check for invalid character inside datafile, and column count mismatch error.
- pre-check can be run separately.

review_comments: Do we need to check other cast error instead of only check string? e.g. no-number string for a numeric field, invalid datatime/date format etc.

right now there're 2 checks: column count mismatch, invalid character

those might be added later.

Should the data sample check parameters also affect the precheck data percentage. I think if I set the percentage to 100% and the both precheck and sample check passed, I will expect a following import should succeed. But, a source line with invalid data type after the first 1000 lines will still cause import failure, with is not expected and anti-intuition.  @sunzhaoyang  what do you think?
BTW, do we allow set `check-requirements = false` in check-only mode?

> BTW, do we allow set check-requirements = false in check-only mode?

yes, check-only doesn't affect logic which depends on this flag

> Should the data sample check parameters also affect the precheck data percentage. I think if I set the percentage to 100% and the both precheck and sample check passed, I will expect a following import should succeed. But, a source line with invalid data type after the first 1000 lines will still cause import failure, with is not expected and anti-intuition. @sunzhaoyang what do you think?

No. As my opinion sample check parameters should not affect the precheck data percentage. If there are some errors occurs maybe we should category them to simple check.  

I don't want to make it complicated to understand.  So the `invalid data type` you mentioned I wish it could be reported by sample check.

In most scenarios, column count mismatch implies all rows count are mismatch. This may output a lot of error logs which is hard to read. I think we should consider merging multiple logs or set a threshold.

```
Besides, if there are many tables and one of the table has more files than others, this check may skip most of the tables. However, sampling more tables seems more better than sampling more files. I suggest sampling every table and perform random file choosing every table.
```
I think this is a scenario that needed to be considered. But we can noted it down first and gather some other feedbacks so we can improve it later.

```
In most scenarios, column count mismatch implies all rows count are mismatch. This may output a lot of error logs which is hard to read. I think we should consider merging multiple logs or set a threshold.
```
Make sense. There may be multiple features could cause huge error messages. I think the better way is to add a common log security  component and not only threshold.  So I suggest we discuss it in a new task.
Since we only check at most one error, I think replace the errChan with common.Once is more ergonimic. In this way, we can just wait d.wg.Wait and then check if there is error occurs.
we need to cancel other routines without error

I think check per file level is not a quite good idea, in case the total file number is not very big but each file is relative big in size, this random logic will result in quite slow speed. How about check the first N bytes of each file?

> How about check the first N bytes of each file?

when there's a large number of files, it's better check a random set of them.

> the total file number is not very big but each file is relative big in size

@D3Hunter You may misunderstand the meaning? I think @glorv means huge file may slow down the total speed.

Besides, if there are many tables and one of the table has more files than others, this check may skip most of the tables. However, sampling more tables seems more better than sampling more files.  I suggest sampling every table and perform random file choosing every table.
@sunzhaoyang have a look

Since `DefaultCSVDataInvalidCharReplace` itself is a valid utf8 charcter, what if the origin input file itself contains this char, e.g, the input file is from an upstream that it does the same replacement for legacy invalid data.
in most case, this should not happen. if it's the case, this check can let user know and check themself.
This message is misleading if `rc.checkTemplate.Output` contains failing items.
success is checking critical failed count, if there're warn failed count, should we take it as `All checks have been passed` @sunzhaoyang
warning should be categories to success and no need to resulting in failed result.

OK. Then, I think we should also take the result of data sample check into consideration. If data sample check failed, I think the check summary result should be fail instead of pass.

BTW, is it possible to also put the data sample check result into the precheck result table? Use a separate log line is not very user friendly.

> OK. Then, I think we should also take the result of data sample check into consideration. If data sample check failed, I think the check summary result should be fail instead of pass.
> 
> BTW, is it possible to also put the data sample check result into the precheck result table? Use a separate log line is not very user friendly.

it is now. In check-only, sample-check and precheck are using the same `checkTemplate`, and precheck doesn't print anything, deferred to sample-check.
why is the check-only config interfering with server-mode?
check-only is used on command line only, check, print result and exit
this does not sound like a blocker requiring check-only and server-mode to be mutually exclusive. in server mode we could "submit a task → check → print result → back to idle" too
check-only is used on command line only right now, maybe we can do it later

This is a invalid check. Given a table schema with a blob(or other binary type) field, its corresponding data in the csv file is likely to be a none unicode string. Thus this check will report false positive result. I think we should only check string fields here.

1. what if table schema contains generated columns?
2. lightning support auto generate default value for missing field if the field has default value
3. How this column check work with `ignoreColumns` feature?

> How this column check work with ignoreColumns feature?

this feature relates to encoding kv, seems not affect checking

Does the current logic can alow import following data?
table schema:
```
create table t (val varchar(16), id int primary key auto_increment);
```

input csv, `test.t.0.csv`:
```
test1
test2
```
no. without header, columns in csv should match ddl
Seems in check only mode, most of the cluster related config fields are useless, do we still need to validate them? E.g, tidb.host, pd-addr, sorted-kv-dir..
we need `tidb.host` to extract ddl from tidb. some config may not needed, but i think it's fine to read/validate them.
Nit: imports don't need to sort into three groups in TiDB repo. ditto for rest files.
goland cann't set per project `imports format` config, painful to switch around(other tools repo needs three groups), will leave it

```suggestion
		select
		{
		case errChan <- errors.Trace(resultErr):
		case <-ctx.Done():
		}
```
not needed, this channel has same size as concurrency
@kennytm what do you think about this. I feel this kind of compaction multi config into one field is not very user-friendly.
@glorv we could use [`flagext.StringsVar`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/carlmjohnson/flagext#StringsVar) here but it only supports the form `--check-only=rate --check-only=rows`
